articleTitle: Artificial Neural Network for STEM-ED in Power Transformer Failure Investigation Based on Power Utility Practice
abstract: This research explores the creation of an educational resource that utilizes STEM principles specifically for teaching computer programming in the field of electrical engineering. The fault analysis simulation program in the research tool integrates the Key Gas and Duval Triangle methods, along with a user-friendly Graphical User Interface. 15 students registered in the computer programming course consisted of the sampling group. The instructional tool had an average score of 4.17 out of 5 famous people which is the highest possible score, in the quality evaluation accomplished by 5 experts. The prepared teaching set satisfied the standard criteria utilizing Meguigans' theory with an effectiveness of 1.1 out of 1. The findings indicated a significant impact on learning performance from the initial assessment to the final assessment, with a significant level of 0.05. Electrical engineering education can be provided effectively with this recently developed teaching and learning tool.

articleTitle: Deep Learning-Based Acoustic Emission Scheme for Nondestructive Localization of Cracks in Monolith Zirconia Dental crown under Load
abstract: This study introduces an innovation non-destructive approach employing dual-sensor acoustic emission (AE) techniques to detect and accurately locate cracks within monolith dental crowns, even when subjected to various load directions. Throughout the process, the AE sensor recorded AE signals that were subsequently converted into .csv data using an AE data acquisition module. Afterward, these digital records underwent denoising to eliminate background and contact-related disturbances. Subsequently, the noise-filtered data underwent processing and classification via a deep learning algorithmic model, enabling accurate localization of cracks within the dental crown. The study utilized AE signals generated by pencil lead breakage (PLB) at the labial, left, palatal, and right surfaces of dental crown for both training and testing of the algorithmic model. Initially, wavelet transform (WT) was employed to analyze and examine the dental crown's location in relation to AE signals. The approach was introduced to precisely identify the sources of AE signals originating from PLB-induced AE events. During the algorithm's training and testing phases, the AE signals were categorized into two groups, and the accuracy of their classification was evaluated. The deep learning-powered AE strategy successfully identified cracks within the dental crown. The total accuracy was 90.625%. This study's innovation resides in its utilization of a dual AE sensor combined with a deep learning algorithm based on AE signals. This combination effectively detects and precisely locates cracks within dental crowns. In contrast to current AE crack-localization methods that depend on human interpretation in radiographic examination, this approach offers an automated and more efficient solution.

articleTitle: Investigation of effect from etching process in fiber refractometer for CO2 measurement
abstract: In this work, a study of power loss within the fiber optic-based refractometer (FOR) due to the chemical etching process has been proposed. The sensing element of FOR with 3 etching lengths: 0.1, 1, and 3 cm, has been de-cladded using a hydrofluoric acid (HF). The output signal during the etching has, continuously, been recorded by a 4-channel data logger. The analytical results showed that the etching length of 0.1 cm is more fragile than the others. It causes the tension of the element making fiber broken. On the other hand, the etching lengths of 1 and 3 cm have more flexible, but large noise exploited. It is due to the environment affected. Besides, the power loss of 48.86%, 87.41 %, and 93.31 % are exploited from all the demonstration lengths. Finally, we might conclude that the etching length the etching length had an inversely proportional to the etched time and direct proportional to the power loss.

articleTitle: Enhancing Sequence Coding Skills in Lower Primary School through Affordable Game-based Learning: A Case Study in Thailand
abstract: This paper presents a case study conducted in Thailand, focusing on the use of affordable game-based learning to improve sequence coding skills in lower primary school students. With the increasing importance of computer science education worldwide, Thailand introduced computer science into its national curriculum in 2018, targeting students as early as grade 1. However, challenges such as the lack of qualified teachers, limited resources, and engaging learning materials still persist in some schools. To address these challenges, this research aimed to provide an affordable learning tool suitable for lower primary school students' programming education. The tool needed to balance the children's skills and motivation while minimizing costs. A programmable robot mouse was selected as the learning tool, allowing students to engage in group activities and develop teamwork skills. Additionally, a coding mat and themed activities were designed to create a fun and engaging learning environment. The research was conducted in collaboration with teachers from Anuban Ban Dek school in Ubon Ratchathani province, focusing on 64 students from grades 1 and 2. The study involved teacher evaluations, student self-evaluations, and pre-test/post-test assessments. The results indicated positive outcomes in terms of students' enjoyment, task accomplishment, and learning comprehension. Furthermore, the pre-test/post-test analysis revealed a significant improvement in students' coding knowledge, with an average score increase of 3.96 points out of 20, representing a 19.8% improvement.

articleTitle: Comparison of Biometric Information During Learning of Visual- and Text-Based Programming Languages
abstract: Novice programmers often start with visual-based programming languages, such as Blockly or Scratch, whereas experts tend to use text-based programming languages, such as C, C++, Java, or Python. However, a seamless transition from a visual- to a text-based language is yet to be established. Our study proposes an approach for this transition by introducing intermediate content with features that bridge the gap between visual- and text-based languages, as demonstrated in our previous study. We also show that incorporating this intermediate content enhances understanding of the text-based language. In this study, we measure learners' biometric information during their course of learning of both visual- and text-based languages, aiming to identify any differences in the biometric information during the training process.

articleTitle: Power Generator Module for Elephant Tracker
abstract: This research studies the development of an electrical power generator module for elephant tracker (PGMET) that is used with the tracking devices for wildlife conservation by The Royal Forest Department Thailand. The proposed module consists of three components: a power generation module, a power storage module, and a power measurement module. The power generation module includes a flexible solar panel and 3 sets of generators that are formed by copper coils and permanent magnets. The research on animal movement was used to design and develop the power generator module. The power generator addresses the problem of the 1-year battery lifetime of the tracking device by extending the operational time to at least 8 years to save cost and increase the efficiency of the non-reusable tracking devices. The electricity-power generator module invention can generate sufficient electricity, at least 3.8V 10W, to power wildlife tracking devices. In the case where the coil and the solar cells are operating at maximum efficiency, both can produce electricity up to 3.8V 12W, which is sufficient for the 24-hours operation demand for the tracking device.

articleTitle: Development of Game-Based Teaching and Learning for Mathmatics and Statistics in Daily Life
abstract: Education is the foundation for both human resource development and educating individuals to be flexible in the future. As a result, the education sector has a clear duty to organize learning for students who exhibit these attributes in order to prepare them for the workforce. Because they are the ones who arrange learning, direct the process, and embed knowledge and behavior in the pupils, the “instructor” is an essential component in attaining these learning objectives. For the growth of learners to acquire such talents, planning and producing learning that covers the topics and achieves desirable features for the learners, as well as the selection of a variety of learning methodologies or teaching, are required. [1], [2] There are several strategies for teaching and learning, one of which is the use of games to promote enthusiasm and interest. Students may enjoy their lessons without feeling tired, enabling them to develop an interest in learning and their own skills. Games allow students to have fun while also helping them build problem-solving and linguistic abilities [3].

Author Keywords: mathematics and statistics in daily life and learning

articleTitle: The Development of Metabolic Syndromes Learning Application Using Augmented-Virtual Reality Technology
abstract: Due to the current era's technology, work, competition, and fast-paced lifestyle, the Thai population lacks exercise and proper healthcare, especially in terms of dietary habits. Metabolic syndrome has become a significant health issue at present, with the number of patients suffering from this condition continuously increasing each year. Raising awareness about the dangers of metabolic syndrome may help solve this problem. Therefore, we designed and developed an augmented-virtual reality (AVR) application to promote learning about metabolic syndrome and evaluate users' satisfaction with it. The data collection process targets two groups of participants: experts in medical media technology and augmented reality (AR)/ virtual reality (VR) development as well as individuals aged between 20 and 40 years. We used a quality assessment questionnaire to collect data from the experts. The assessment included evaluating the accuracy of the media content and the quality of the AVR application. Pre- and post-test was conducted to compare knowledge levels before and after using the application among a group of users. Additionally, a user satisfaction survey was conducted to gather feedback on the media's educational content related to metabolic syndrome using AVR technology. The results demonstrate that the accuracy of the media content was rated at an excellent level, while the overall application design was rated at a good level, according to the experts. Users' satisfaction with the application was also considered good. The statistical analysis showed a significant improvement in knowledge levels after using the application, based on the pre-and post-test comparisons. In conclusion, users expressed high satisfaction with the application and gained significant knowledge about metabolic syndrome, as supported by statistical evidence.

articleTitle: Preliminary study effect of hydrogen peroxide on properties of mung bean protein isolates for producing plant-based emulsion sausage
abstract: This study aimed to use hydrogen peroxide (H<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>O<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>) to decolorize mung bean protein isolate (MPI) for producing plant-based emulsion sausages. Bleached MPI was obtained by dispersing mung bean protein concentrate (MPC) in 0.5% H<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>O<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> at a ratio of 1:10 for 90 min, at 30 °C before alkaline extraction and acid precipitation. It was found that H<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>O<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> had no significant effect on protein content, water holding capacity (WHC), oil absorption capacity (OAC), and emulsion stability (ES) but significantly lightened the color of MPI and sausage. MPI sausages had higher gel strength than commercial soy protein isolate (SPI) and H<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>O<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> bleached MPI sausage gave the highest gel strength.

articleTitle: StudyScape: A Development of a Simple Collaborative Learning Environment Using a Cloud Application Platform
abstract: Web-based collaborative learning has gained popularity as a learning approach in higher education including the development of various web-based environments. Effective use of web-based collaborative learning can facilitate students' learning. Prior to the COVID pandemic, a web-based learning approach was mainly utilized in life-long learning, distance learning, and informal learning. During the global pandemic, web-based learning was almost the only way. This paper presents the development of a web application, called StudyScape, that could be used as a platform in a collaborative learning environment. As a small-scale low-cost proof-of-concept, StudyScape utilizes a free platform as a service that facilitates building, running, and operating the implemented application entirely in the cloud together with another free cloud-hosted database. The StudyScape has many features that provide users with essential social web application functionalities such as posting files, commenting and bookmarking posts, adding like, prompting notifications, launching a real-time chat, and searching. As a result, this web application exhibited satisfactory functionalities to be used as a learning ecosystem.

articleTitle: Current-Mode Universal First-Order Analog Filter Using CCCIIs
abstract: This paper presents a new current-mode first-order universal analog filter using current-controlled current conveyors (CCCIIs). The proposed circuit can realize first-order sections such as all-pass, low-pass, high-pass filters with both non-inverting and inverting transfer functions into single topology. The pole frequency of these filters can be controlled electronically. The output terminals possess high impedance level which is required for cascading of current-mode circuits. The proposed analog filter is verified using SPICE simulation. The CCCII has been simulated using the 0.18 µm CMOS technology with a supply voltage of 1.8 V. The simulation result can show that it agrees well with theory.

articleTitle: Development of Competency-Based Curriculum in Off-Grid Solar Cell Installation Work Using IoT Technology for Energy Monitoring
abstract: The paper aims to present the development of a competence-based curriculum for off-grid solar installation using IoT technology to enhance the installation and operation skill as well as the application of IoT technology for energy monitoring. The research data is collected from a training course in four-years student with a target group of 30 undergraduate students of electrical engineering and education program in electrical power major. The research findings indicate that the tasks, abilities, behavioral objectives, skills, content, exercises, and assessments of the curriculum align cohesively. The evaluation of the curriculum of suitability in terms of details, usability, and content relevance indicates the highest level of suitability. Additionally, the satisfaction assessment results of course users were at a highest level. The assessment of the developed curriculum's effectiveness meets the criteria of E1/E2, achieving an efficiency score of 86.41/86.89 respectively, demonstrating its high performance.

articleTitle: Developed Skills with Business Simulation Game
abstract: Does learning accounting information systems through a business simulation game really build relationships among developed skills, perceived knowledge, and reality? The objective of this research is to primarily measure the attitude of perceived skills among students from vocational schools who voluntarily participated in the training program. The opinions were gathered from students enrolled in classes such as accounting software, accounting processes, and accounting profession seminars. The results revealed a high level of positive attitude towards the use of ICT in accounting information systems, perceived skills, perceived knowledge, and reality.

articleTitle: A Design and Development of Learning Innovations for Training Courses on Smart Greenhouse Systems
abstract: This article aims to design and develop a learning innovation for a training course on a smart greenhouse system for Thung Yai Sarapee Learning and Innovation Center at Songkhla Rajabhat University. There are two objectives of this research. First, to create innovative materials for training courses and second, to assess the quality of the learning innovation package. The process of designing and developing innovative training materials consists of two main parts. The first part is the design of the smart control system. The second part focuses on designing learning content. After developing the innovative media, an expert assessment was conducted. Five experts evaluated the innovative media developed and the overall evaluation results of all topics were appropriate at a high level (mean = 4.45 and S.D. = 0.55). Similarly, the assessment of learning content for all topics was also highly appropriate (mean = 4.45 and S.D.= 0.51). These findings suggest that the learning innovations created in this research have the potential to effectively support individual training in smart greenhouse systems.

articleTitle: Customized CMU-CDIO Syllabus for Engineering Students at Chiang Mai University: Design and Piloting
abstract: This paper presents an approach for customizing essential attributes for engineering students at Chiang Mai University based on the CDIO syllabus 3.0, resulting in the “customized CMU-Eng CDIO syllabus.” The syllabus facilitates planning of student activities by departments, student development affairs, and the student union involved in developing students' social skills. The paper discusses the process design, and pilot survey of the customized CMU-Eng CDIO syllabus. The preliminary findings from three stakeholder groups, including the faculty staff, student unions and industries, indicate the importance of skills such as analytic reasoning, problem-solving, teamwork, collaboration, and communication. The student development staff recommends additional competencies related to mental health and self-awareness. The Thai version of the proficiency evaluation rubric is developed by translating the syllabus into Thai, altering the language for comprehension, and tailoring to fit industry context as suggested by the industrial pilot groups.

articleTitle: Visual Perceptual Ability and Academic Achievement in Undergraduate Engineering
abstract: Cognitive and neurosciences provide new ways to advance the scholarship of learning and teaching. One such application is identification of the cognitive processes that contribute to academic achievement. Intelligence testing has been shown to be of limited use in higher education, and so there is a need to identify other cognitive and neurobehavioral factors that may be important. One possibility, in the context of STEM education, is visuospatial ability, as this has been linked to achievement in several technical, or things-based courses. In the current study, 60 industrial engineering students and 60 social sciences students were assessed on a task of visual size judgement, and the ability of performance to predict grade point average (GPA) scores was estimated. It was found that size judgement was significantly and positively correlated with GPA within the engineering group, but not in the social sciences group. Furthermore, the results could not be explained by demographic factors such as sex or age. It is concluded that visual perceptual ability, specifically size judgement, may be a useful predictor of academic achievement, and may thus help to partly explain why some engineering students excel, and others do not. Furthermore, potential for training of visuospatial skills to enhance attainment in engineering training is discussed.

articleTitle: From Needs to Goals - The Development of CALL Materials (Using Content-based Instruction for Undergraduate Students Studying English for Careers)
abstract: The study aimed to investigate the effectiveness of the current English for Careers curriculum and identify material development needs. CALL materials using Content-based Instruction were developed for Radio and Television Broadcasting-majored students based on their needs. Data were collected through questionnaires and interviews. The findings revealed that 1) in terms of exposure to the English language, surfing the internet was shown to be the most popular activity; 2) over half of the participants found only some of the topics could improve their English proficiency; and 3) listening and speaking were perceived to be two of the most important skills needed to advance their careers. This justified the strong need for material development. Based on Brinton's CBI framework (2003), English for Careers lesson plans were designed and validated by experts to ensure efficiency.

articleTitle: Automatic Alcohol Hand Sanitizer by Applied Electronics Circuit with Two Prototypes
abstract: Hygiene for humans is necessary to maintain human health to keep the body clean and free from germs. Including not wanting to spread the disease to various places, especially during this time with the spread of COVID-19 in increasing numbers. Viruses continue to evolve species to be able to reproduce and survive. For this reason, this research article, therefore, designed and invented an automatic liquid alcohol dispenser in two prototypes to prevent germs from spreading from the hands of people. Users would not have to touch any part of these devices when using them. The prototype I is better than prototype II in terms of the range of operation, measurement precision to dispense an amount of alcohol, and overall scores of users' satisfaction. Finally, prototype I has more advantages than prototype II. However, if we concern about cost, prototype II is better. To get more performance in prototype II, the performance will be improved by a new circuit designed to get more stability.

articleTitle: Reinforcement Learning application on Gamification
abstract: Machine Learning, a component of Artificial Intelligence, has gained increasing importance and contribution to our society. This paper presents one of many machine learning methods, Reinforcement Learning, through gamification of a simple maze game. The purpose of this paper is to visualize the basic concept of reinforcement learning and strategy which the reader may be able to apply. The paper compares two model-free learning algorithms: on-policy and off-policy approaches using SARSA and Q-Learning models. Our experiments will demonstrate the difference between on-policy and off-policy by training the agent on mazes of different scales and complexity. Moreover, this paper will also illustrate the effect of Epsilon Greedy Policy. The maze is generated and visualized using Pygame. The result is presented in a table and graph plot for comparisons.

articleTitle: Online Robotics Learning STEM Activities for Robot and Packaging Design Camp
abstract: This paper introduces an online robotics learning STEM activities for the robot and packaging design camp to develop soft skills in knowledge management. The main purpose is to contribute the understanding of robotics and packaging design, how to use product and packaging design principles to build a Tiger cardboard robot, that can inspire youth to pursue education in robotics engineering with industrial design and packaging. This camp is two course content from online STEM activities such as: robot and packaging design contents. There are 18 students participating in the camp. Pretest and posttest on the content of both courses are used in project-based learning evaluation. The results demonstrate that learner outcomes can reach the 15.6% baseline.

articleTitle: Feasibility Study of An Underpass Tunnel Construction at Silpakorn University
abstract: This work is a feasibility study of an underpass tunnel construction project at Silpakorn University based on a case study using cut-and-cover tunnel construction method. The project income is evaluated from estimated accident damage while the expenses consist of initial, operating, and maintenance costs. Consequently, both income and expenses are utilized as input variables, with the project lifetime of 20 years and 5% of discount rate. Moreover, the basic financial tools - namely net present value (NPV), internal rate of return (IRR), benefit-cost ratio (BCR), and payback period (PB)- are applied to find the investment feasibility. After analysis, the calculated NPV, IRR, BCR, and PB are 124,973,599.62 THB, 7.60%, 1.22, and 14 years and 5 months, respectively. Therefore, the project is feasible for investment and also cost-effective. Furthermore, sensitivity analysis shows that the project has low sensitivity, therefore suitable for investment in Thailand, where inflation rate fluctuation is low.

articleTitle: The study of academic achievement in the General Physics II course of undergraduate students intervened by personalized reduction of prior fundamental knowledge deficit
abstract: In this research, we investigated the impact of a tailored intervention on our undergraduate students enrolled in the General Physics II course who displayed a deficit in specific fundamental knowledge aligned with their high-school standard curriculum in Thailand. First, we assessed students' prior fundamental knowledge deficits using pre-lesson tests to gauge their academic preparedness in specific topics based on the Thai Institute for the Promotion of Teaching Science and Technology (IPST)'s curriculum. We found that the concerning level of deficit in most of the topics. After we administered the complementary exercise, the custom-tailored assignments to address each student's specific knowledge gaps, we evaluated their academic achievement in advanced course content and found their post-lesson above the 50% passing criteria. Our findings indicated a significant enhancement in their academic achievement. This study provides insight into a more structured approach for assessing students' specific fundamental knowledge and implementing remedial measures before introducing more complex course materials.

articleTitle: The Development of Teamwork as Soft Skill with Cooperative Learning in Song Translation for Enhancing the 21st Century
abstract: Teamwork played an important role for soft skill. It enhanced the effective work in the 21<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">st</sup> century. The purposes of this research were 1) to examine the development of university students toward teamwork as soft skill with cooperative learning; 2) to compare the students' song translation ability before and after using cooperative learning; and 3) to investigate the strategies of song translation from Thai into English. The sample was 22 second-year students in English teaching program, faculty of education, Phranakhon Si Ayutthaya Rajabhat University, selected by purposive sampling. The research instruments were 1) Teamwork Skills Questionnaire (TSQ), 2) pre-test and post-test, 3) a questionnaire measuring satisfaction on cooperative teamwork, and 4) in-depth interview. The quantitative data was analyzed by frequency, percentage, mean, standard deviation, and dependent t-test. The qualitative data was analyzed by using of content analysis. The findings were 1) For the teamwork's ability, the students had more adaptability, coordination, decision - making, leadership, interpersonal, and communication. The students' satisfaction toward cooperative teamwork was at a high level with the average of 3.48; 2) The average scores of post-achievement test was higher than the before one. It was significant at the .05 level. The majority provided positive responses both questionnaire and interview; and 3) There were main 3 strategies of song translation: translation, adaption, and replacement, respectively.

articleTitle: Integrating Blended Learning and Collaborative Learning to Develop Reading for Main Idea for English Teaching Program Students
abstract: In the 21<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">st</sup> century, reading proficiency is a critical skill, and the ability to discern the main idea is crucial for enhanced reading comprehension. However, this can be a challenging skill for ESL learners to master. It's therefore imperative to foster the development of reading skills. Techniques like blended learning and collaborative learning can be particularly effective in nurturing these skills, including the ability to identify the main ideas. This study aimed to 1) to compare learning achievements before and after learning with blended learning and collaborative learning and 2) to evaluate the ability of reading comprehension through blended learning and collaborative learning. Research instruments used in this research included lesson plans, pre-test and post-tests, and a reading evaluation form. The study was conducted with a group of 28 first-year Education students at Phranakhon Si Ayutthaya Rajabhat University in English Teaching Program. Findings demonstrated that students' aptitude in pinpointing the main ideas improved significantly after teaching via blended learning and collaborative learning methods, and they achieved a high level of proficiency in this area.

articleTitle: Comparing Coverage Models of Radar: Evaluating Viewshed Against Ground Truth Detection
abstract: This paper aims to enhance the assessment methods of radar effectiveness in surveillance and air command and control systems. It involves a comparison of different radar coverage models to explore their operational aspects. The study utilizes actual radar data for analysis and modeling, with the goal of creating a comprehensive coverage model for target detection. The computed coverage areas are then compared using the Viewshed technique. The results provide valuable insights that can guide the utilization of radar data for maintenance, repairs, and performance enhancements of radars within the broader air defense system. Additionally, a proposed guideline can be useful for offering strategic planning recommendations for radar system installation for improving the gap coverage of radars.

articleTitle: The Development of English Course Material for STEM Learners Entitled “Technical English for Engineering Students”
abstract: This paper was aimed to develop and evaluate the quality of the English course material for STEM learners entitled “Technical English for Engineering Students” and to examine the satisfaction of the students towards the course material. The panel of 3 experts was formed in order to evaluate the quality of the course material. The research tools consisted of a) quality evaluation form for the expert panel, and b) questionnaire on the students' satisfaction towards the English course material with Likert's 5-point rating scale. The statistical methods were mean score and standard deviation. At the end of the course, 207 first-year undergraduate students who enrolled in the course “Technical English” filled out the questionnaire on their satisfaction towards the course material. The findings showed that the expert panel gave positive review comments about the course material in terms of the communicative approach to English language teaching (ELT) and features of English for specific purposes (ESP). Furthermore, the students expressed the highest level of satisfaction towards the course material.

articleTitle: Video Production Design by Using Project-Based Learning of Pre-Service Teachers
abstract: Videos are an important tool for teachers in the digital era since they can deliver teaching content in the form of multimedia. It is a fantastic learning experience for learners to learn through seeing and listening. Furthermore, video production is convenient and may be readily and widely used on social media. As a result, pre-service teachers must have the information, abilities, and ability to construct video products in order to assist their future teaching. Project-based learning is a method of encouraging instructor and students to have knowledge of video design and production. Students must have a plan for working, practicing, collaborating, and seeking self-awareness. It is a method that promotes creativity, learning abilities, and communication skills in order to attain long-term learning success. The purposed of this research were to study the design of video production using project-based learning and to compare the learning achievement of pre-service teachers. The population and sample consisted of pre-service teachers from the Faculty of Education, Phra Nakhon Si Ayutthaya Rajabhat University. Research tools included lesson plans, video production design assessment forms, and tests. The statistics used for data analysis were Mean, Standard Deviation and t-test. The findings revealed that pre-service teachers could design video productions at a high level (x =3.79, S.D.= 0.77). They had a statistically significant higher learning achievement after learning than before learning at the. 05 level.

articleTitle: Academic English Word Counting and Classifying System with Web Application and LINE OA
abstract: In writing an academic paper, it is crucial to use appropriate academic vocabulary and an adequate amount of academic terms. The initial way to assess the level of academic writing in a document is by analyzing the frequency and usage of academic terminology. This preliminary examination can provide valuable insights into the academic vocabulary employed in the paper. In this work, the development of an academic word counting and classifying system in English is done utilizing the Academic Word List (AWL) sublist families as the database. The system was created using Python language and libraries such as spaCy, Bootstrap, and Heroku. The proposed system is accessible through web and LINE applications and has been proven to be effective in counting and classifying words, checking message similarity, and matching the words with the academic word list. It is found that this system could serve as a valuable tool for enhancing the quality of academic writing and reviewing academic documents.

articleTitle: Personal OKRs: A Tool for Academic Goal Setting
abstract: This study aimed to implement the Objectives and Key Results (OKRs) framework as a Personal OKRs training program tailored for first-year students facing challenges in setting academic goals. The program involved a workshop and biweekly progress reviews. Sixteen participants, first-year undergraduate students who had previously taken preparatory courses in mathematics or physics, took part in the study. Six students received the Personal OKRs training program for sixteen weeks, while ten students comprised the control group without intervention. The impact of the Personal OKRs program on students' academic achievement and the three goal-setting components (meaningfulness, personal improvement, and data-based) were examined. Results indicated a marginally significant effect of the intervention on the data-based component (<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$t$</tex> (14) = -1.97, <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$p= 0.07$</tex>) with a large effect size (<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$d=1.05$</tex>). Regularly tracking progress and engaging in self-reflection during the intervention appeared to play a significant role in enhancing academic goal setting.

articleTitle: Gender Equality in STEM Workforce: A Survey-Based Approach
abstract: This study examines the challenges faced by women in Myanmar's technology sector and explores their experiences and aspirations. The findings reveal that these women encounter various obstacles, including limited mentorship support, gender discrimination, and unique difficulties related to pursuing job opportunities overseas. Safety concerns amidst the country's current situation also serve as a significant motivator for seeking employment abroad. Social networks play a crucial role in job acquisition, but women face greater challenges in accessing professional networks compared to men. The male-dominated environment in the industry results in a lack of workplace mentors for female participants, hindering their professional growth. The study underscores the importance of implementing comprehensive measures to support women in the tech industry, including promoting gender equity, improving workplace support, addressing safety concerns, and providing access to mentorship and training programs. Considering the impact of Myanmar's current situation, providing stability, security, and opportunities for professional growth are crucial for women's career decisions and aspirations.

articleTitle: The Lesson Learned to Reinforce Learning Process for Developing Village Educational Volunteers in Marginalized Area
abstract: KMUTT initiated the development of a mechanism called “Village Educational Volunteers (VEV)” by planning the recruitment of youth who have graduated high school and reside in the village. The project's primary objective was to enhance the quality of education and promote occupational development. At present, six individuals are actively engaged as village educational volunteers (VEV). Their responsibilities encompass assisting children and youth with specific learning needs, both in classroom settings and within the community. They play a crucial role in creating lesson plans, delivering instruction, and closely monitoring small group activities and the progress of individual children, offering guidance and support to those facing behavioral challenges. Additionally, VEV collaborated with the community to develop some learning modules that incorporate STEM subjects. Almost every day, VEV operates within the community environment, focusing on education in rural areas, committing to this noble cause for approximately one year. Reflecting on their experiences as VEV, several key lessons have been identified. They expressed concerns about how best to help children from diverse backgrounds achieve their learning goals and how to enhance their professional skills and knowledge for personal development. Moreover, VEV recognizes the need to acquire additional skills, such as facilitation techniques, creative thinking, and understanding child psychology, to ensure sustainable support for marginalized areas in the future.

articleTitle: Sensing Probe Development for Pulse Wave and Blood Pressure Detection using Fiber Optic Based Fabry-Perot Interferometer
abstract: A low-cost sensing probe based on fiber optic Fabry-Perot interferometer (FFPI) was designed and developed for pulse wave and blood pressure measurements. The FFPI system was comprised of the light source, sensing probe, and photodetector. To develop the sensing probe, four reflective materials and also three elastic materials were demonstrated to measure the reflectivity and elasticity, respectively. Furthermore, the probe was tested on the fingertip and neck to obtain the interference fringes with five times of repeatability. Besides, the peak detection and fringe counting techniques were employed to demodulate interference fringes into pulse waves. The results revealed that Aluminum-coated mirror provided the highest reflectivity, while a latex rubber balloon, the most elastic material, had a percentage of elongation of 199.25 mm and a Young's modulus of 2.85 MPa. To conclude, the sensing probe had the ability to detect heart pulses, paving the way for an affordable, painless, and user-friendly instrument.

articleTitle: The Development of Online Training Models to Promote Game-Based Learning Teaching Skills and Development of Game Applications on the Android operating system
abstract: The research objective were to: 1) develop online training model to promote game base learning teaching skills and developing game applications on the android operating system. 2) to study the effect of using an online training model to promote game base learning teaching skills and developing game applications on the android operating system. The sample groups of the research were 30 the third-year students with a bachelor's degree from program in Electrical Engineering and Education, Department of Teacher Training in Electrical Engineering, King Mongkut's University of Technology North Bangkok. Research instruments include training tools, game-based learning activities tools, measure and evaluate tools. The research results shown that 1) the efficiency of online training model had the efficient of 92.41/86.40 higher than the 80/80 criteria, 2) the results of application development skill scores of trainees trained with online training model were significantly higher than before training at the. 01 level, 3) teaching skills scores of the trainees had an average of 81.68 and 4) the trainees had an opinion on online training model at a high level (mean = 4.13, S.D. =0.21)

articleTitle: The Analysis of the Maximum Efficiency for Delivering load and Total Energy loss of an Electrical Transformer Based on 22 kV
abstract: This article presents an analysis of the maximum efficiency for delivering load and total energy loss of an electrical transformer. The electrical transformer in this case study has a rated voltage as 22 kV, rated apparent power 50 - 100 kVA, which can be operated with the electrical distribution system of the provincial electricity authority (PEA). However, this electrical transformer is composed a no load loss and a load loss, respectively. These losses directly influence to the efficiency and energy loss of 3 phases electrical transformer. As mentioned above, this article is shown to analyze the maximum efficiency by using the practical parameters. Moreover, the total energy loss of an electrical transformer is determined, because it can be transferred to the electricity cost.

articleTitle: Training the Trainers in Elementary and High Schools on IoT Using Design Thinking Approaches
abstract: This article describes how the authors apply and implement teaching methods using design thinking approaches to train in IoT (Internet of Things). The purpose of this study is to determine how well of design thinking with IoT topics to teachers and students, and how we could improve teaching or coaching strategies. Participants in this study are the researcher as the trainers, 20 to 30 teachers from different schools and 20 to 30 on each high school student (Grade 9 to Grade 12) as the trainee perform group projects. By collecting observations from trainee's activity outcome on each step of design thinking approach to deliver problem solving projects with IoT, the researcher applies narrative analysis to interpret patterns or characters on each activity. Each approach involved with activities which develop teachers or students to make their own learning and understanding problem and complete their IoT prototype projects within 4–5 days. Not only electronics devices and embedded systems and programming are used but also recycled materials. LEGO alike blocks are setup for learning activities corresponded to levels of students and available school resources. Different sets of learning activities in this article are adjusted attributable to education levels and individual school resources. From the analysis after the trainings, the conclusion shows how the researcher can improve by applying appropriate hardware/software in learning activities on different education levels and apply the design thinking more efficiently in teaching or coaching teachers and student in schools.

articleTitle: Investigating DPST high school students' responses in a STEM activity: How to measure tomato ripeness
abstract: The STEM activity: How to measure tomato ripeness allow DPST students to apply what they already learned from laboratory enrichment subjects in physics, biology, chemistry, technology, and mathematics to solve it. Participants were 10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">th</sup> high school graders of DPST in academic year 2021 and 2022. The objectives of the research are: (1) How did the students use their learned knowledge in laboratory enrichment subjects to tackle the question: how to measure tomato ripeness? (2) What were strengths and weaknesses of students' projects? Results show that students' responses in the STEM activity demonstrated their application of knowledge and skills from the laboratory enrichment subjects to the activity with the use of multiple and single subjects to tackle the problem. The groups of students in 2021 performed better at identifying problems and selecting measurement. Nevertheless, students of academic year 2022 did better on planning and executing a project based on scientific knowledge.

articleTitle: A Case Study on AAC Implementation; Funjai Application
abstract: FUNJAI, an Augmentative and Alternative Communication (AAC) application, was developed to facilitate those in need of assistance with their daily life communication. Currently, there are several AAC applications present with English versions, however, access is very limited in Thailand. Authors have implemented FUNJAI as a Thai AAC application that is free to download across iOS and Android platforms to ease the struggles of non-verbal neurodiverse in Thailand. FUNJAI is established using Flutter for software development and Figma for the design and appearance of the application. Essentially, the developed FUNJAI application has been tested with AAC's teachers and users which are found to be very easy to access and use as it has been implemented based on real user experience. The Application has been successfully implemented and tested by experience teachers.

articleTitle: The Enhancement of Problem-Solving Abilities with The Usage of CDIO and A3 Thinking to Reduce Waste in PCBA Manufacturing
abstract: The current study aimed to develop a learning framework using Conceive, Design, Implement, and Operate (CDIO) and A3 Thinking to enhance problem solving abilities in Printed Circuit Board Assembly (PCBA) manufacturing. Moreover, this research focuses on reducing the waste from PCBA production. The participants were employees in the position of leader who was responsible for overseeing the PCBA production line. In the treatment, participants would brainstorm ideas to analyse the problems by finding the root cause of the problem and identifying solutions. The employees also, find methods to avoid repeating the same problems, conducted in the form of PDPC (Process Decision Program Chart). The current results found that the employees can develop the ability to solve problems occurring in the PCBA manufacturing process, and they can reduce PCBA manufacturing waste by around 57.78%.

articleTitle: Instruction Model of Electrical Motor Control for Up/Re-skill New-staff's APM Argo company
abstract: This paper has proposed the training of electrical motor control system for practice new staff at industrial APM Argo CO.,LTD. in Chombueng district Ratchaburi province. Due to work skill of new staff there aren't enough. As the problem, effect to efficiency working in process such as more spent work time, team work not as well. Thus, this paper has studied the instruction model of motor control up/re-skill for new staff of APM Argo company. With instruction model have designed it can support the new staff by training. From the study, found that the efficiency of the instruction model was effective according to the Meguigans quality criterion valued at 1.154, in which standard more than 1.00. that imply was this instruction model had high efficiency. By the way, the quality of the instruction model as a high appropriation, with a total mean of 4.10 and a standard deviation of 0.62 respectively.

articleTitle: Effects of Wheat Flour, Wheat Starch, and Modified Starch on Cassava Starch Substitution and Crispness of Crackers Experiencing High Relative Humidity
abstract: This study investigates the effects of wheat flour, wheat starch, and modified starch as cassava starch substitutes, along with their respective amounts, on the physical properties of deep-fried crackers. Additionally, the physical quality of the crackers, including external structure, water activity (aw), bulk density, and hardness, is examined under high relative humidity conditions. Various formulations of crackers were prepared, and their external structure, moisture content, density, and hardness were analyzed. The results revealed that crackers with 15% and 20% wheat flour substitution exhibited smaller and more evenly distributed pores on their surfaces compared to the control formula. Incorporating cross-linked starch led to a smoother surface with smaller and more dispersed air pockets. The wheat flour formula had the highest moisture content and showed a lower density, indicating favorable puffing characteristics. Texture analysis showed that the hardness of all formulations increased over time. The controlled formula exhibited the fastest increase in hardness, indicating that it became firmer and more fracture-resistant. Furthermore, crackers with an aw of 0.15 experienced water migration when exposed to high relative humidity, leading to a transformation from a glassy state to a rubbery state. However, the formulations with wheat flour and cross-linked starch delayed this transformation, maintaining crispiness for an extended period.

articleTitle: Solar Cell System Simulation for Renewable Energy Learning Innovation
abstract: The research aims to develop a solar cell system simulation for renewable energy learning innovation. Active Learning with STEM education is used in the teaching and learning method. The research instruments include a solar cell system experimental set, a solar system simulator, an assessment form, and a questionnaire. The research methods are divided into four steps: Analysis, Design, Development, and Evaluation. The research findings revealed that the five experts' view of appropriation in utilizing the solar cell system simulation for learning was of high suitability, and the satisfaction of ten users was also of high level. Finally, the solar cell simulation system for learning can be used effectively in the learning and teaching of science and technology courses.

articleTitle: The Conceptual Framework for Designing an Appropriate Learning Approach to Improve Students' Achievement for Educational Opportunity Expansion Schools Using Digital Learning Platform
abstract: Classrooms serve as a realm of imagination and optimism for students who face constraints in their educational expeditions. Hence, it is a priority for students to consider and promptly seek assistance from their teacher. Numerous methods of integrating educational technology to uphold learning are widespread due to the influence of technological advancements, global pandemics, and constraints in the educational sphere. Hence, there is a demand to alter the state of both teaching and learning from their initial forms. Previously, our primary emphasis was solely on classroom instruction, but due to these constraints, online education has gained significant significance. One of the strategies referred to as Blended Learning involves integration between online and face-to-face learning supported by educational technology. It is becoming more prevalent. Accordingly, the teacher's perspective should possess the capability to effectively utilize blended learning, connecting online and face-to-face learning through the assistance of educational technology. Enhancing students' accomplishments to broaden educational access, thereby enhancing schools for an elevated educational standard.

articleTitle: Automatic Solid Waste Collection Prototype From Drainage Pipe Based On Solar Energy
abstract: This research aims to develop and evaluate the effectiveness of the automatic solid waste collection prototype from drainage pipe based on solar energy in order to decrease the amount of debris in the river. The main concepts of this proposed prototype are to filter the solid waste from the drainage pipe and transfer them into the proper container. Two types of system controls, which are the automatic control and the manual control, were proposed. Both control systems were carefully designed to use the renewable energy stored in the battery in order to improve system's capability in the night time. The experimental results show that both control systems of the proposed prototype perfectly function. For the manual control, the proposed machine can operate anytime depending on user's needs and can effectively filter most of the solid waste before flowing into the river. For the automatic control, the DC motor can only run under conditions that infrared proximity sensors detected solid waste on the belt conveyor and the waste level in the container is lower than the threshold level. Thus, the detected solid waste will be moved to the container by the belt conveyor. Therefore, the benefit of automatic control system can maintain the heat causing by running motor because the belt conveyor will be driven for 15 seconds each time. By using Line application, the alert system can function at 100% accuracy.

articleTitle: Integration of Data Literacy in Electrical Engineering Education
abstract: This paper describes our efforts to enhance data literacy among electrical engineering students, considering the rapid growth of modern loads like electric vehicle chargers and renewable energy generators in electrical distribution systems. To effectively utilize smart grid technology, electrical engineers must possess strong data analysis and machine learning skills. However, the current electrical engineering curriculum faces challenges such as uncoordinated regulatory frameworks and limited hands-on experiences. We present two case studies that demonstrate the integration of data literacy through workshops and a hackathon for engineering students. The outcomes of these initiatives were evaluated through the achievements of participants, as assessed by industry experts.

articleTitle: The Development of Artificial Neural Network Model for Predicting Optimal Job Position in Quality Control Station
abstract: The workforce in the manufacturing sector often works that do not match their competencies or are transferred to unskilled jobs such as quality control employees, leading to prolonged training periods and increased inefficiencies. This study aims to address this issue by analyzing the required employee competency by skill mapping. The competency dataset was obtained through the researcher's evaluation and job description documents, classifying the employees' knowledge and hard skills. An artificial neural network model was developed to predict the employee position in the new product quality control station. The study utilized the perceptron neural network algorithm for supervised learning in machine learning. The attributes were knowledge and hard skills and were divided into training and testing sets. The model was trained using RapidMiner program and its performance was measured using a confusion matrix. The results of using confusion matrix in the development of this prediction model resulted an accuracy of 82.00%

articleTitle: Study of Investment Feasibility for Smart Bus Stations at Silpakorn University
abstract: This work is an analysis of investment feasibility of smart bus stations at Silpakorn University. The proposed consists of 4 main parameters: initial cost, operating cost, maintenance cost, and equipment rental income, respectively. Consequently, those variables are used to analyze the investment value incorporated with the economic analysis tools, such as NPV, IRR, BCR, DPB, etc. Furthermore, we assigned that the project has a lifetime of 10 years, and a discount rate of 5.50%. In addition, the sensitivity analysis is also conducted with a service rate from 0 to 3 THB, and equipment rental income of 1,200,000 THB per year, with a 2.6% increase in the service rate every 3 years. The analyzed results indicated that the construction of the smart bus stations project is suitable to worth the investment. Finally, it could be concluded that the project has more convenient to invest with a service rate of 2 THB.

articleTitle: Mobile Learning: The Using Learning Media of Science Teacher Students and Their Perspectives on Mobile Learning
abstract: This research aimed to: 1) investigate the using learning media in mobile learning of science teacher students, and 2) investigate the perspectives of science teacher students regarding mobile learning media. The sample consisted of 18 third- year science teacher students, at Phra Nakhon Si Ayutthaya Rajabhat University, the second semester, the academic year 2022, who were studying the subject of creating and utilizing scientific learning media and were selected using a purposive sampling. The research instruments included an observation form and focus group interview form. Collecting data involved observing teacher students' behavior during instruction and group discussions. Data collection was the content analysis. The findings of the study revealed that students utilized mobile learning media such as applications, online forum, simulation programs, virtual programs, websites, and online videos. Utilizing media was intended to assist students in achieving their learning objectives. According to student feedback, mobile learning media could motivate students to study and create an enjoyable learning environment and help students achieve better learning results. The advantage of this study is useful element for science teacher students or teachers of all disciplines to bring these media as guidelines for learning management for students according to the objective of mobile learning media.

articleTitle: Guidelines for Competency Development in Automation Projects by Microcontroller for Computing Science Teachers
abstract: The objectives of this research were to, 1) study the guidelines for competency development in automation projects by microcontroller for secondary school computing science teachers, 2) utilize the guidelines for competency development in automation projects by microcontroller, to establish a training curriculum for secondary school computing science teachers, and 3) study the utilization results of the guidelines for competency development in automation projects for secondary school computing science teachers, which are divided into 3.1) Comparison of the mean achievements in knowledge and understanding in the field of automation projects by microcontroller before and after training, of the secondary school computing science teachers, and 3.2) To study the satisfaction of the secondary school computing science teachers who attended the training curriculum on competency development in automation projects by microcontroller. Target groups of the study was 20 secondary school computing science teachers who voluntarily participated in the project by specific method. The study methodology was to review literatures and researches, interviewed the professionals and relevant personnel. Afterwards, synthesizing the content of the obtained data, developing the draft training curriculum through feasibility study by various stakeholders, which included academics, researchers, school managements and teachers. Statistics used in this study, such as, mean and percentage. The study result showed that 1) the guidelines for competency development in automation projects by microcontroller comprised of the following competency indicators, which are 1.1) Engineering foundation, such as automation and equipment operation, and basic tools using, 1.2) knowledge of industrial foundation (electrical-electronics), 1.3) working of microcontroller with fundamental projects, 1.4 Working of microcontroller coordinating with advanced projects), and 1.5) Application of automation projects in factories or daily life. 2) Training curriculum draft of competency development in automation projects by microcontroller of 12 hours, consisting of the training topic which covers the studies following item 1.3) The study result, on the application of the guidelines for competency development in automation projects for secondary school computing science teachers, can be divided into 3.1) Mean achievement, in knowledge and understanding of the automation projects by microcontroller, after training was higher than before training of the secondary school computing science teachers and 3.2) The study result of satisfaction of the secondary school computing science teachers, who has attended the training course on competency development in automation projects by microcontroller, were at the level of very good.

articleTitle: A Conceptual Modification Design for the Commercial Small Rice Milling Machine
abstract: A small rice milling machine is wildly used by farmer in Thailand of many purposes such as a reservation, a commercial or a nutrition purpose. After the Covid-19 situation, many companies want to recovery their own business. Many strategies were applied and one of their strategy is to modify their own product. This project was started to modify the commercial small rice mill from A R C GLOBAL CO., LTD. To serve their customer's requests survey. There are three main topics that need to be improved 1) the milling rate 2) rice and broken rice sorting and 3) the waste sorting. A strategy which is applied to modify the commercial small rice mill, is easy and less modification. The machine was disassembled and observed its mechanism. Finally, the milling and the sorting mechanism were modified. The simulation result shown that the milling rate is improved to become 120 kg/hr. and the sorting mechanism can sorting the rice, broken rice and waste. Finally, the owner purposed were satisfied by this conceptual design to improve their product. The good products for commercialize mean the functional with the easy manufacture.

articleTitle: A Design and development of learning using aircraft basic computer simulations
abstract: This academic essay was created for A Design and development of learning using basic computer models of airplanes. Used to create instructional materials. To solve the fundamental aircraft challenge of two groups of students with disparate aircraft backgrounds. by the objective of testing students' knowledge two groups 120 students must have completed Senior High School and a Diploma/High Vocational Certificate. Using a learning simulation tool to measure skills before and after learning for two groups of students for comparison. The first group has a rudimentary understanding of airplanes. The second category has no aircraft as a foundation. Using aircraft basic computer simulations to measure the results of the five skills tests in 2022–2023. 75% of all skill tests were passed by all 120 pupils. Accidents and equipment damage are cut in 50%.

articleTitle: The Effect of Preprocessing on U-Net for Bladder Segmentation in CT Images
abstract: This research proposes preprocessing techniques for computed tomography (CT) slices with the aim of improving the performance of a deep-learning segmentation model (U-Net model). The preprocessing techniques used in this study include window leveling, histogram equalization, Gaussian blurring, and cropping (incorporating mathematical morphology and histogram projection). The U-Net model is applied to three groups of input data sets (B-I to B-III) for training, validation, and testing. The segmentation performance is evaluated using metrics such as Dice similarity coefficient (DSC) and intersection over union (IoU). The trained U-Net model achieves the highest DSC (95.15%) and IoU (91.09%) under B-III dataset, utilizing cropped and enhanced CT input datasets. Window leveling, histogram equalization, Gaussian blurring, and cropping are identified as the optimal preprocessing techniques for bladder segmentation. This novel research applies diverse image processing techniques in medical image preprocessing to enhance the deep-learning U-Net model's segmentation performance.

articleTitle: Color shade classification using RGB sensor
abstract: This paper presents the design of an RGB sensor system for classifying similar color objects using color shades as an alternative to using a camera, which can be relatively expensive. The RGB sensor is employed to capture the reflected color of the object and then calculate the amount of color concentration in red, green, and blue on a scale of 0–255. The number 255 represents the highest possible concentration of the color, while number 0 indicates no representation of that color in the object image. As a result, when using the RGB sensor to classify different shades of the object, it achieves a success rate of 75.12%, as calculated from experiments in the shade of yellow color. The RGB sensor can be used to help reduce labor costs and increase rate of efficiency in various industries such as in food industrial, medical lab, and more.

articleTitle: Application of Augmented Reality with On- The-Job Training for The Quality Control Workforce
abstract: The product testing process in the electronics industry is an essential part that verifies the product's quality before it is delivered to the customer. However, the workforce often has limited knowledge and skills for working in the product testing process, resulting in high breakdown time. Therefore, this article presents the development of augmented reality (AR) technology combined with on-the-job training to enhance the workforce's skills for the product testing process. AR was designed to simulate a step-by-step product testing environment, supplementing the real world. It offers a comparison between the correct and incorrect testing processes and allows for product zooming and rotation to provide clear details of the operation. Additionally, a sound button was added to explain each step-in detail. During daily product testing, the workforce can use AR through their phones to scan the target paper provided by the trainer. The virtual environment would then be demonstrated, and the workforce can adjust the testing process steps according to their abilities. After implementing the AR application, the workforce answered a survey indicating that the AR technology was easy to use and helped them better understand the testing process. Comparing traditional training and AR, the error rate was reduced by 0.6% using AR. The results also showed a decrease in errors from product testing and helped reduce the breakdown time caused by the faulty product testing process.

articleTitle: CFD Simulation of Flow Inside A Closed-loop Oscillating Heat Pipe with 11 Turns
abstract: This research deals with CFD analysis on the thermal performance of passive two-phase fluid flow in a closed-loop oscillating heat pipe (CLOHP) with 11 turns in the evaporator and condenser section. The 3D CLOHP is a 2 mm inner diameter tube with a length of evaporator, adiabatic, and condenser sections equal to 50 mm. Water is used as a working fluid with filling ratios of 50%. The simulations are performed using three-dimensional ANSYS Fluent software, employing the pressure-based solver for solving the continuity and momentum equations and the Volume of Fluid (VOF) method for phase interface capturing. A temperature-dependent model for the mass transfer between phases due to evaporation and condensation is employed. The separate phase compression model is utilized for the VOF simulations, and the flow simulations are conducted to determine the thermal resistance and heat transfer rate of the CLOHP. The temperature of the evaporator and heat flux of the condenser are set in each simulation case. The fluid flow pattern inside the CLOHP is reflected by changes in volume fractions of the liquid-vapor phase in three regions: evaporator, adiabatic, and condenser. Comparing simulation results to Charoensawan's experimental results, it was found that the thermal resistance is consistent with the experimental within the maximum deviation of 15.30 %. The thermal resistance decreased as the evaporator temperature and heat transfer rate increased. The thermal resistance decreased significantly in the last 2 cases of evaporator temperatures, 358.84 K (85.69 °C) and 370.04 K (96.89 °C), respectively.

articleTitle: Outcome Based Capstone Project Design Assessment: a Case Study on an Electrical Engineering Program
abstract: Design experience is an important component for all engineering curriculum to prepare students for engineering practice. An ABET-accredited engineering curriculum is required to culminate “a major design experience based on the knowledge and skills acquired in earlier course work and incorporating appropriate engineering standards and multiple realistic constraints.” A capstone project is a significant part of an overall framework of outcome-based education in engaging electrical engineering students in engineering design process. This article demonstrates an example of an assessment framework used in Capstone Project courses in electrical engineering program at Mahidol University. The assessment, which was created based on ABET student outcomes and educational objectives, is used to ensure that student design projects incorporate stakeholders' requirements and other relevant design aspects, and to instill professional attributes in students as well as to drive the continuous improvement of the courses and the program according to outcome-based education framework.

articleTitle: Professional Competency Development Using Self-Directed Learning via On The Job Training
abstract: In the industry, interns perform tasks that closely mirror regular employees. However, they often need a clearer understanding of their roles, leading to a development of competency. Therefore, this article aimed to applying self-directed learning via on-the-job training to develop interns' professional competencies and career awareness. This learning model includes two steps: firstly, identifying the work areas of interest for interns was conducted. Experienced staff would share insights about their careers. The second step focuses on technical skill development. Interns would gather information from on-the-job training. Staff members would clarify the work process to enhance interns' understanding. Interns wound learn from practice by completing tasks. Additionally, they would rotate through several sites to exchange knowledge. The current results indicated that the interns had a high degree of self-awareness regarding their skill development. These interns have improved their specialized tool usage skills. And gained awareness of job aspects of interest for the future.

articleTitle: A Conceptual framework for Developing Soft Skills As the Required competencies for Engineering Inspectors
abstract: This article presents a conceptual framework for the development of soft skills as the required competencies of third-party engineering inspectors. Previous studies have found that the soft skills play an important role as the required competencies of engineers. These skills also enhance competitiveness, international recognition, consistency with the changing world as well as applicability for the actual work contexts. However, a lack of a clear guideline for developing soft skills especially in engineering inspectors could be observed. Moreover, each organization would provide soft skill trainings to personnel on an as-needed basis only. As a result, no practical standards were in place. To develop soft skills for engineering inspectors, this study proposes a conceptual framework consisting of 6 steps, namely, analyzing soft skills, selecting required soft skills, prioritizing soft skills, soft skill development process, soft skill evaluation, and preparation of relevant documents. This framework is expected to further create a soft skill development model which will be appropriate for engineering inspectors in Thailand.
